answer: A tide of cheap fake agents can be held back by requiring each identity to stake a refundable deposit that only unlocks after months of honest work, like a relic locked in a vault. A newcomer must also earn endorsements from established agents who lose part of their own stake if their protege cheats. Forging one fake identity is cheap, but forging a thousand that each lock funds and risk a sponsor's stake costs far more than any single scam can repay, while an ivory-tower registry run by one central approver would be a single point of failure.
